properties.name: The wall check is served — the import-boundary walk a consumer can find, run and be told about, with a gate that notices a capability promising reach it does not have
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
THE CAUSE, walked with the root-cause skill (fact:root-cause-the-wall-check-was-generalised-in-code-and-never-in-reach-and-the-checkout-cannot-feel-it): tools/wall_check.py had every leg for this repo and none a consumer needs. find_tools indexes MCP tools only; no skill named it; the kit does not carry it; allocated to a served component while realized only by an unserved script; and this checkout cannot feel any of that because it has the file. A consumer re-wrote the analysis by hand 25 days after it was built and filed it as "unknown". The first plausible cause — "the kit tarball" — was measured and refuted: an init-installed project has tools/ on disk and still cannot reach it.

THE FIX AT THE CAUSE, three legs for the consumer:
SERVED — `wall_check` MCP tool (crates/reflow2-mcp/src/wall_check.rs, tools/built.rs). The script is compiled into the binary via include_str! (the skills' pattern), written to a scratch dir at call time and run with python3 against a fresh export of the LIVE design, cwd = the project root (the directory the graph store sits under; `root` overrides; the report names the root it used). Stdout is the report; `budget_chars` bounds it with a stated cut; a missing interpreter or a non-zero exit is refused with the cause, never an empty report. Nothing about the analysis changed.
NAMED — check-health and adopt tell the agent when to reach for it, in the user's words (all three skill trees).
GATED — tools/check_consumer_reach.py: a realized Capability whose text claims reach beyond this repo, realized only by tools/ scripts, fails the build. The shipped tools/ files are read off release.yml's kit-copy lines, not a hand list — its first run flagged the machine-wide installer, which release.yml DOES copy into the kit, and corrected the defect record's own sentence about kit contents. OBSERVED FAILING on the unfixed export (the wall check, and only it) before the capability was re-linked.

PINNED, observed failing first: the find_tools instance pin ("does my declared decomposition match the real coupling…" → wall_check in the top 5) FAILS with the #[tool] attribute removed and passes with it. Four integration tests (find, a real run over two registered files with an undeclared import, nothing-registered says so, budget honoured) and three unit tests (missing interpreter refused with what to do, root resolution, bounding).

RECORDED BESIDE IT: dec:reflow2-serves-source-reading-analyses-that-report-and-never-write, accepted on Anthony's word ("I'd like to fix this for all 4"); the other three analyses from the field report await their definitions in the user's terms.

NOT DONE HERE: porting the instrument to Rust (a python3 on PATH is already assumed by the loop-nudge hook every consumer runs).
